    <section class="prose-section" id="ai-adoption"><p class="eyebrow">QUT · Future Skills Organisation · 2025–2026</p><h2>Generative AI adoption by Australian workers</h2><p class="role">Principal Investigator &amp; Project Lead · $229,531 commissioned study</p><p>This national study examined how workers use generative AI and what support they need from employers. I led the study, coordinated the research team, co-design and working group engagement, and subsequently developed the findings into resources for employers.</p><p>The work involved a <strong>41-member national AI Research Working Group representing 36 organisations</strong>, spanning government, unions, professional bodies, universities and employers of different sizes.</p><p>Working group members represented organisations including the Digital Transformation Agency, National Artificial Intelligence Centre, Commonwealth Bank, Woolworths Group, Suncorp, Australian Council of Trade Unions, Australian Industry Group and the Council of Small Business Organisations Australia (COSBOA). <a href="https://www.futureskillsorganisation.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/AI-Research-Working-Group-Membership.pdf">See FSO’s published membership list ↗</a></p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>A national research report, stakeholder workshops and co-design sessions, and an employer-support toolkit released as a working web application and downloadable resources for organisations building AI literacy, workforce capability and readiness.</p><p>The research and employer-support resources have since informed further adaptation and engagement with SMEs, including FSO’s SME AI Coach.</p><div class="project-links" aria-label="FSO project resources"><a class="text-link" href="https://www.futureskillsorganisation.com.au/supporting-generative-ai-adoption-by-workers-the-role-of-employers/">Research report &amp; employer resources <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a><a class="text-link" href="https://www.futureskillsorganisation.com.au/sme-ai-coach/">SME AI Coach resource pack <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></div><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>AI adoption</li><li>Workforce capability</li><li>Employer resources</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p><strong>QUT / ARC BITA:</strong> I led the team with Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan and Dr Stephen Whyte, with coordination and administrative support from Jen Petley.</p><p><strong>Future Skills Organisation:</strong> Michelle Circelli, Timothy Burt, Peta Skujins and the broader FSO team collaborated on the original project. Siobhan O’Sullivan has supported the subsequent stage and engagement with SMEs.</p></div></details></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="knowledge-platforms"><p class="eyebrow">QUT research collaborations · 2026–present</p><h2>Research software for archives and scientific interviews</h2><p class="role">Principal Investigator &amp; Project Lead</p><p>I lead two projects that help researchers search source material and check information extracted from it.</p><article class="project-entry" id="spanish-inquisition"><h3>Spanish Inquisition archival research platform</h3><p>With collaborators at QUT, Universidad de Oviedo, Universidade da Coruña and QUT eResearch, I’m developing software to search historical judicial records and extract information for analysis. I lead the project and supervise technical development. Extracted records retain links to the original documents so researchers can check them.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>An access-controlled research application deployed in a QUT-supported environment, with structured extraction and links back to the archival sources.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Archival research</li><li>Semantic retrieval</li><li>Structured extraction</li><li>Human verification</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Tim Nguyen, an ARC BITA research assistant, undertakes the main software development under my supervision. The QUT / ARC BITA research team includes Professor Benno Torgler, Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan and Dr Douglas (Tony) Beatton, with deployment support from QUT eResearch.</p><p>International collaborators include Professor David Matesanz Gómez (Universidad de Oviedo) and Andrea Teira Fachado (Universidade da Coruña).</p></div></details></article><article class="project-entry" id="web-of-stories"><h3>Web of Stories scientometrics platform</h3><p>This platform lets researchers search interviews, videos and transcripts from prominent scientists. It links people and concepts across the material, helping researchers trace scientific relationships and the development of ideas.</p><p class="note">Access to both live web applications is currently restricted through QUT’s network. The research team intends to make them publicly accessible in the future.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>An access-controlled research application deployed in a QUT-supported environment, connecting interviews and transcripts through retrieval and knowledge graph workflows.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Scientometrics</li><li>Knowledge graphs</li><li>Scientific interviews</li><li>Source provenance</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Tim Nguyen, an ARC BITA research assistant, undertakes the main software development under my supervision. The QUT / ARC BITA research team includes Professor Benno Torgler, Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan and Dr Douglas (Tony) Beatton, with deployment support from QUT eResearch.</p></div></details></article></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="simulation"><p class="eyebrow">QUT · Queensland Department of the Premier and Cabinet · 2023–present</p><h2>Behavioural simulation for public decisions</h2><p class="role">Chief Investigator &amp; Project Lead</p><p>I lead research and stakeholder engagement on combining synthetic populations, behavioural evidence and agent-based modelling to investigate vulnerability, resilience and decisions in disaster management and crime prevention.</p><p>My responsibilities include MPhil supervision, technical coordination and engagement with government and industry research partners.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>Applied AI and behavioural simulation platform development, with research demonstrations delivered in April 2026.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Synthetic populations</li><li>Agent-based modelling</li><li>Public decisions</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Arian Mashhady, an ARC BITA / QUT MPhil student, undertakes the main software development and research under supervision from me, Professor Benno Torgler and Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan, with additional support from Dr Douglas (Tony) Beatton.</p></div></details></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="other-research"><p class="eyebrow">Government, industry &amp; university collaborations</p><h2>Evidence for policy and practice</h2><article class="project-entry" id="ip-australia"><h3>Drivers of AI Investment · IP Australia</h3><p>Co-author of a 2023 commissioned study connecting workforce skills, job advertisements and patenting activity to investigate AI investment and innovation.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>A published commissioned research report for IP Australia.</p><p><a href="https://www.ipaustralia.gov.au/tools-and-research/professional-resources/data-research-and-reports/publications-and-reports/drivers-of-ai-investment">Read the published IP Australia report ↗</a></p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>AI investment</li><li>Workforce skills</li><li>Innovation policy</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>The research team comprised Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan, Professor Uwe Dulleck, Professor Benno Torgler and me, with partner support from Annita Nugent and Michael Falk at IP Australia.</p></div></details></article><article class="project-entry" id="riskwise"><h3>RiskWise · AI-assisted qualitative analysis</h3><p>As Applied AI Research Lead, I led conceptual design and contributed to technical development of a workflow for scalable, traceable qualitative coding. It combines semantic automation, language models, human review and provenance-linked outputs, and has been applied to <strong>more than 4,250 Australian agricultural research, conference and extension artefacts</strong>.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Qualitative coding</li><li>Semantic automation</li><li>Human review</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>With Tim Nguyen and Dr Germán Puga and Professor Marit Kragt at the University of Western Australia.</p></div></details></article><article class="project-entry" id="ai-copilots"><h3>AI copilots, work and professional identity</h3><p>I lead a QUT ethics-approved longitudinal study, developed with Inspired Education Australia, examining how enterprise AI copilots affect work practices, capability, identity, trust and collaboration in Queensland high schools.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>In progress</strong>An ethics-approved longitudinal study of enterprise AI copilots in Queensland high schools.</p><p><a href="publications.html">Browse related research outputs →</a></p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Longitudinal research</li><li>Work practices</li><li>Professional identity</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p><strong>Study in progress:</strong> Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan, Professor Benno Torgler, Dr Douglas (Tony) Beatton, Arian Mashhady and me at QUT / ARC BITA, working primarily with Rashan Senanayake at Inspired Education Australia.</p></div></details></article></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="surveylm"><p class="eyebrow">Panalogy Lab · Independent applied AI R&amp;D · 2023–present</p><h2>SurveyLM</h2><p class="role">Co-Creator &amp; Research Lead</p><p>I co-created SurveyLM, a web platform for exploring how different audiences might respond to ideas, products, policies and communications. Researchers configure synthetic populations using constructed profiles and approved demographic or behavioural data, then run surveys, controlled experiments and “what-if” scenarios across groups and models.</p><p>It supports early exploration of alternatives, including questions or audiences that can be costly or difficult to study. Teams can compare wording, imagery and scenarios, challenge assumptions and identify questions for targeted human research. I test where simulated responses agree with human evidence and where they miss variation or depend on modelling choices.</p><p>I lead research and experimental design, contribute to software development, and maintain the public application and its cloud deployment. SurveyLM has been live since <strong>September 2023</strong>.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>A live research platform, public technical report and peer-reviewed applications, with free academic access supporting empirical validation and user feedback.</p><p class="platform-snapshot"><span><strong>46</strong> registered accounts</span> <span class="snapshot-separator" aria-hidden="true">·</span> <span>Approximately <strong>A$3,500</strong> in voluntary user donations</span> <span class="snapshot-separator" aria-hidden="true">·</span> <span>Over <strong>US$12,500</strong> in AWS Activate credits</span></p><p class="metric-source">October 2026 platform snapshot. AWS credits are non-cash hosting support; donations are voluntary user contributions.</p><div class="survey-resources"><div class="project-links" aria-label="SurveyLM resources"><a class="button" href="https://surveylm.panalogy-lab.com/Platform">Open SurveyLM <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a><a class="text-link" href="https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2308.00521">Read the technical report <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></div><details class="project-detail"><summary>Use &amp; adoption</summary><div><p>Registered accounts include researchers affiliated with QUT, the University of Bayreuth, Universidade da Coruña, the Federal University of Espírito Santo and the Institute of Swiss Economic Policy. Researchers affiliated with Maastricht University, the Laboratory for Innovation Science at Harvard and WHU have also used SurveyLM. Academic access is free to support validation, feedback and ongoing improvement.</p><p>Current evaluation includes the Behavioural Insights Team’s testing for Queensland road safety research and work with Tales of Tomorrow GmbH on film and series genre, format and theme combinations across synthetic audiences. Other studies explore disaster response scenarios, workplace health, safety and environment change, psychological safety interventions and biomedical governance policy pretesting.</p><p>Related commissioned advertising and behavioural research through QUT / ARC BITA totalled approximately <strong>A$60,000</strong> for a major Australian insurer.</p><p>Researcher controls include configurable populations, image-based and other multimodal designs, sequential and group interactions, cross-model comparisons, and structured exports for statistical and econometric analysis.</p></div></details><details class="project-detail"><summary>Hosting, models &amp; data</summary><div><p><strong>Hosting and maintenance:</strong> I maintain the public browser-based application on AWS Lightsail in Northern Virginia, USA (us-east-1). Inference processing locations depend on the selected model provider and endpoint.</p><p><strong>AI models:</strong> SurveyLM combines Panalogy-developed software with third-party pretrained language models. Current integrations include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek and Z.AI. We do not currently train foundation models for SurveyLM.</p><p><strong>Data handling:</strong> Simulations use constructed profiles, approved aggregate data and authorised business materials. Inputs may be sent to selected third-party endpoints for inference. Panalogy does not use customer data for training or fine-tuning by default; any such use requires separate agreement and authorisation. Provider training-use, retention and processing terms are reviewed per endpoint. Data minimisation, access, encryption, deletion and incident-response requirements are agreed before confidential data is introduced.</p><p><strong>Enterprise configurations:</strong> Australian-region or private hosting, regional or private inference, API access, enterprise authentication, additional connectors and custom endpoints can be scoped. This includes providers such as OpenRouter and client-approved fine-tuned model endpoints. Storage, logs, backups, subprocessors and residency requirements would be verified for each configuration.</p></div></details><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Synthetic populations</li><li>Behavioural experiments</li><li>Model evaluation</li></ul><details class="project-publications"><summary>Peer-reviewed studies <span>2 articles · 2025</span></summary><ol><li><a href="https://doi.org/10.1108/JSM-11-2023-0441">Comparing human and synthetic data in service research: Using augmented language models to study service failures and recoveries <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a><span>Journal of Services Marketing · 39(1), 36–52 · Compared SurveyLM responses with five human experiments, documenting context-dependent agreement and limitations.</span></li><li><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbusres.2025.115318">Using reminders with reward opportunities to reduce spectator no-show behavior <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a><span>Journal of Business Research · 193, 115318 · A field experiment accompanied by complementary synthetic treatment checks.</span></li></ol></details><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Co-created and developed with Dr Son Tran and Bang Dao (Panalogy Lab), with research and empirical input from Professor Benno Torgler and Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan.</p></div></details></div><p class="note">I presented our augmented language model work and showcased Panalogy Lab at Something Tech / Something Fest in Brisbane in 2023.</p>

    <section class="prose-section" id="industrial-ai"><p class="eyebrow">Panalogy Lab · Industrial applications</p><h2>Industrial and physical AI</h2><article class="project-entry" id="agent-rung"><h3><a class="project-product-link" href="https://panalogy.ai/technology/agent-rung">Agent Rung <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a> · Industrial control intelligence</h3><p>An industrial fault diagnosis and decision-support system combining live PLC data, vendor-specific knowledge and safety-oriented reasoning.</p><p><strong>My contribution:</strong> defining industrial use cases and requirements with engineering partners, and coordinating deployment with the technical team.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Deployed</strong>Industrial fault diagnosis and operational decision support at industrial sites in Australia.</p><p class="reported-outcome"><strong>Field-reported examples:</strong> Across three Australian oil and gas, aluminium production and water-treatment sites, reports include discovery of a 13-year-old emergency-stop wiring fault, a diagnostic task estimated at 3–4 hours completed in 20–30 seconds, and live integration in minutes without a shutdown.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>PLC data</li><li>Fault diagnosis</li><li>Operational decisions</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Primarily with Dr Son Tran and Latzi Marian at Panalogy Lab.</p></div></details></article><article class="project-entry" id="icebreaker"><h3><a class="project-product-link" href="https://panalogy.ai/technology/icebreaker">Icebreaker <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a> · Virtual production supervisor</h3><p>A manufacturing decision-support system combining production line modelling, a language model reasoning agent and natural language queries of production data.</p><p><strong>My contribution:</strong> scoping the project with the industry partner, defining operational requirements and coordinating the engineering and software work.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Pilot</strong>Initial work at a food and beverage manufacturing plant on the Gold Coast. Broader deployment remains under development.</p><p class="reported-outcome"><strong>Partner-reported results:</strong> Hopper batch-error margins reduced from ±5–8 kg to ±1 kg at a 200 kg setpoint, with 6–7-minute cycles and 120 operating hours per week.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Production modelling</li><li>Manufacturing</li><li>Decision support</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Primarily with Dr Son Tran and Latzi Marian at Panalogy Lab.</p></div></details></article></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="business-intelligence"><p class="eyebrow">Panalogy Lab · Knowledge systems</p><h2>Business and document intelligence</h2><p>GAIA and Expert Recommender apply document intelligence, structured extraction, semantic search and knowledge graphs to business information and expertise discovery.</p><article class="project-entry" id="gaia"><h3><a class="project-product-link" href="https://panalogy.ai/technology/gaia">GAIA <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a> · Connected organisational knowledge</h3><p>I work with the Panalogy Lab team on GAIA, which transforms fragmented organisational documents into connected, searchable knowledge graphs. It combines information extraction, knowledge representation and semantic retrieval to uncover relationships across documents and support source-grounded questions, research and AI workflows.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>MVP delivered</strong>A document and business intelligence MVP developed through an AI readiness and scoping engagement for a national engineering services provider.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Document intelligence</li><li>Knowledge graphs</li><li>Semantic retrieval</li><li>AI agents</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Developed with the broader Panalogy Lab team, particularly Dr Son Tran and me.</p></div></details></article><article class="project-entry" id="expert-recommender"><h3><a class="project-product-link" href="https://panalogy.ai/technology/expert-recommender">Expert Recommender <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a>  · Evidence-based expert discovery</h3><p>I lead the development of workflows for identifying and matching relevant expertise, working with research colleagues and an intern I supervise. The work combines structured evidence, semantic matching and network analysis to identify experts based on their research, experience and connections, beyond conventional keyword searches.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>Recommender systems</li><li>Semantic matching</li><li>Network analysis</li><li>Expertise mapping</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Primarily with Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan, Professor Benno Torgler and an intern I supervise, within the broader Panalogy Lab team.</p></div></details></article></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="readiness"><p class="eyebrow">Panalogy Lab · Verbrec · 2025</p><h2>Organisational AI readiness</h2><p class="role">Project Lead</p><p>I led an AI readiness and implementation scoping study across a multi-site engineering services organisation. Interviews and focus groups informed the prioritisation of AI pilot opportunities, requirements definition, business cases, cost and schedule estimates, and implementation roadmaps. Governance advice and documentation were informed by ISO/IEC 42001 and Australia's Voluntary AI Safety Standard, with reporting and board-level decision materials supporting investment and implementation planning.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>An organisational AI readiness assessment, prioritised pilot opportunities, scoped requirements, implementation roadmaps and governance-informed decision materials to guide AI investment and adoption.</p><p><a class="text-link" href="https://panalogy.ai/case-studies/ai-scoping-roadmap">Read the Verbrec AI scoping and roadmap case study <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Project focus"><li>AI readiness</li><li>Use-case prioritisation</li><li>Business cases</li><li>Delivery planning</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Led by me with contributions from the broader Panalogy Lab team, working with staff and leadership at Verbrec.</p></div></details></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="engineering"><p class="eyebrow">AEP Elical · 2018–2023</p><h2>Engineering in operational environments</h2><p class="role">Electrical Engineer, Project Manager &amp; Business / Quality Leadership</p><div class="site-visit">
